title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.

findings.explanation: The diff does not introduce any SQL queries. The code uses Django ORM with parameterized queries (.get(id=rule_id), .filter(project=project)) which are safe against SQL injection. No raw SQL strings or string concatenation in SQL contexts is present.

The authorization check for IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) has been improved. The convert_args method now properly filters rules by project before retrieval: for AlertRule it uses fetch_for_project(project), and for Rule it filters by project=project. This ensures a user cannot access rules from projects they don't have access to. The endpoint inherits from ProjectEndpoint with ProjectAlertRulePermission, which validates project access. The test_cannot_mute_unowned_alert() test confirms the fix works by verifying a user cannot access another user's organization's rules.

evidence.content:
def test_cannot_mute_unowned_alert(self):
    user2 = self.create_user("foo@example.com")
    org2 = self.create_organization(name="Other Org", owner=user2)
    project2 = self.create_project(organization=org2, name="Other Project")
    self.login_as(user2)
    response = self.get_error_response(
        org2.slug,
        project2.slug,
        self.issue_alert_rule.id,
        target="everyone",
        status_code=404,
    )
    assert response.data["detail"] == "Rule does not exist"
